import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style for the plot
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

    y='price_usd',

    style='has_video_4k', 
    palette='deep', 
    markers={0: "X", 1: "o"},
    alpha=0.7
)

scatter.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=14)
scatter.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14)

# Customize legend
handles, labels = scatter.get_legend_handles_labels()

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style for the plot
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between price and megapixels, colored by sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=cameras, 
    x='megapixels', 
    y='price_usd', 
    hue='sensor_type', 
    style='has_video_4k', 
    palette='deep', 
    markers={0: "X", 1: "o"},
    alpha=0.7
)

# Add labels and title
scatter.set_title('Digital Cameras: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=16)
scatter.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=14)
scatter.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14)

# Customize legend
handles, labels = scatter.get_legend_handles_labels()
scatter.legend(handles=handles[1:], labels=labels[1:], title='Sensor Type & 4K Video', fontsize=12)
